_comment: Lawn visit photo shot list (lawn report rebuild P18, GATE_LAWN_SHOT_LIST). The one definition shared by the server (server/services/lawn-photo-shots.js) and the admin client (client/src/lib/lawn-photo-shots.js). Order is the order the technician sees. key is the value stored in lawn_assessment_photos.zone (a free string, no enum). areaWeight is the weight a photo carries in a legacy area-score merge (0 = detail shot, never moves an area score); an unlabeled photo counts as 1. heroRank orders the report's lead photo (higher wins, then photo quality). pairable shots are the same spot every visit and may pair across visits for the before/after slider. max is how many photos one visit may carry for that shot. guide is the model-facing one-liner the lawn visit prompt prints for the shot (lawn report rebuild P19a); supportsCause marks the close-ups a named cause may rest on (absent = false). recheckPairable marks the shots whose SAME SPOT is identifiable across visits, so the paired-photo recheck may compare them (lawn report rebuild P19b; absent = false). It is separate from pairable, which only drives the before/after slider: front (the mailbox or driveway apron) and back (the back door or lanai edge) are fixed spots; side does not record which side of the property it shows, so two visits can show opposite sides and it stays out until a stable side identity is captured.
sizeNote: maxPhotoBytes is the per-photo limit (decoded bytes, 5 MiB, same as the request validator). maxTotalBytes caps one visit's photos together (decoded, 30 MiB): 30 MiB of photos is 40 MiB as base64, which leaves 10 MiB under the 50 MiB /api/admin JSON body limit for the rest of the request, so a contract-valid set of 8 never meets a parser-level 413. A resized 1600 px JPEG is about 0.3 to 0.5 MiB, so a normal set uses well under a fifth of this.

shots.label: Front overview
shots.instruction: The whole front from the same spot as last time (mailbox or driveway apron), chest height, house corner in frame.
shots.feeds: Scores coverage, color, weeds; anchors the before/after.
shots.guide: Whole front lawn from a fixed spot at chest height, house corner in frame.

shots.label: Back overview
shots.instruction: Same rules from the same back door or lanai edge.
shots.feeds: Second area sample so one side never speaks for the lawn.
shots.guide: Whole back lawn from the back door or lanai edge.

shots.label: Side overview
shots.instruction: Down one side strip from the front corner. Use when the back is gated or blocked.
shots.feeds: Stands in for the back overview.
shots.guide: A side strip of the lawn; stands in for the back overview when the back is blocked.

shots.label: Canopy close-up
shots.instruction: Straight down, 12 to 18 inches up, at a typical spot (not the worst), hand or gauge for scale.
shots.guide: Straight down from 12 to 18 inches at a typical spot (not the worst); shows true color and weed identity.

shots.label: Blade and crown
shots.instruction: Part the grass, 4 to 6 inches away, blade plus the runner and crown.
shots.feeds: Leaf spot, chinch, webworm and thatch live here.
shots.guide: Grass parted at 4 to 6 inches: blade plus runner and crown, where leaf spot, chinch bug, webworm and thatch show.

shots.label: Hot edge
shots.instruction: Turf along the driveway, sidewalk or curb in afternoon sun, 6 to 10 feet of edge.
shots.guide: 6 to 10 feet of turf along a driveway, sidewalk or curb in afternoon sun, where chinch bug and drought start.

shots.label: Shadiest turf
shots.instruction: The most shaded patch, 10 to 15 feet wide.
shots.feeds: Keeps thin shade from reading as disease.
shots.guide: The shadiest patch of turf; keeps thin shade from reading as disease.

shots.label: Problem area
shots.instruction: Whenever something looks wrong: one wide shot with good turf beside the bad, one close-up of the patch edge.
shots.feeds: The named finding only. Up to 2 photos.
shots.guide: The named problem: a wide shot with good turf beside the bad, or a close-up of the patch edge. Up to 2 photos.
